body:
As a workaround when you alias complex fields you need to declare the types you'd like returned into the type map.

``` php
$query->selectTypeMap()->types(['time' => 'time'])
```

The ORM can infer type information for column names in the schema, but not for columns that are aliased/defined with custom functions.

I think inferring types for simple aliases should be doable.
@markstory given how simple it is to tell a query the type of a custom column, I'd rather not infer it magically
@lorenzo I don't think it is a significant effort to do type inference on simple aliased columns. I was only thinking of inferring types for columns that are defined in the table schema.
@markstory funny enough, I just realise I use the aliasing to avoid the casting in some cases!
@lorenzo Interesting, so we'd have another situation where fixing one problem would create another.
yeah, but admittedly, my usage is a hack.
Ok, I'll put together a pull request for the aliasing I had in mind. We can see how offensive it is.

issue.title: Add result type casting for simple column aliases.

issue.body:
When columns in the schema are aliased to other fields we can easily and correctly infer the result set types. Doing this makes the result sets consistent when columns are aliased and when they are not.

Refs #9402
